explanation: First normal form is violated when a column contains multiple values for the same fact. The usual fix is to move the repeating fact into a separate related table so each row contains a single email address.

options.text: Leave the table as is and require semicolons between email addresses
Create a separate `SupplierEmail` table with one row per email address and a supplier reference
Add more columns such as `email2` and `email3` to the `Supplier` table
Store only the first email address and discard the rest

prompt: A `Supplier` table has columns `supplier_id`, `name`, and `contact_emails`. The `contact_emails` column sometimes contains multiple email addresses in one cell. Which design is the best first-normal-form fix? Assume you still need to keep all email addresses for each supplier.
reviewConcept: Use related rows for repeating facts so each column remains single-valued.

source.title: Normalization and other Data Modeling Methods
